definitions.definition: Water removed from a surface-water or groundwater source.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: Do not label as consumption; once-through cooling can dominate withdrawals while returning most water.

definitions.definition: Water evaporated, transpired, incorporated into products or crops, consumed by people or livestock, or otherwise removed from the immediate water environment.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: A return flow can be degraded or spatially displaced without being consumptive use; quality needs a separate indicator.

definitions.definition: Water withdrawn by a public supplier before treatment, distribution, and delivery to customers.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: Customer deliveries are components of this withdrawal and cannot be added to it.

definitions.definition: Water withdrawn directly by the user from a source rather than delivered by a public supplier.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: USGS industrial totals cited here are self-supplied and omit public-supply deliveries.

definitions.definition: Water used at the facility or end-use location.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: For data centers, direct cooling/humidification water and indirect electricity water must be shown separately.

definitions.definition: Upstream water attributed to electricity, fuels, materials, or other inputs.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: Use for attribution. Do not add to national withdrawals if upstream sector withdrawals are already included.

definitions.definition: Maximum design production rate under stated conditions.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: Desalination and AWG capacities are not annual yields and do not demonstrate reliability.

definitions.definition: Modeled renewable water generated or available through natural hydrologic processes for the defined spatial and temporal unit.
definitions.dashboard_guardrail: Definitions differ by assessment; managed storage, imports, transfers, reuse, and groundwater mining require explicit treatment.

comparable_products.geography: United States plus territories as documented
comparable_products.best_use: National sector/source snapshot and 1950–2015 withdrawal trend
comparable_products.do_not_use_for: Claiming current 2026 use or complete national consumptive use

comparable_products.categories: Crop irrigation, public supply, thermoelectric power
comparable_products.best_use: Time-varying withdrawal and consumptive use for three sectors
comparable_products.do_not_use_for: A complete national total across manufacturing, mining, livestock, aquaculture, and self-supplied domestic use

source.locator: Release summary and linked data products

comparable_products.categories: Natural supply, demand, and stress indicators
comparable_products.do_not_use_for: Predicting utility failure or assigning an aquifer depletion year

aggregation_rules: National 2015 category withdrawals may be summed only within a single Circular 1441 table and boundary.
PP1894-D 2010–20 modeled values may be summed across its three covered sectors but must be labeled covered-sector subtotal.
Direct data-center water may be compared with national sector flows after unit conversion; indirect electricity water must be separately allocated.
A desalination-equivalent plant count is a scale illustration, not a siting, cost, energy, brine, or permitting feasibility assessment.
Plastics water savings require a product-service counterfactual and cannot be calculated from industrial withdrawals alone.
